Henry Louis `` Buster '' Gehrig ( born Heinrich Ludwig Gehrig ; June 19 , 1903June 2 , 1941 ) was an American baseball first baseman who played 17 seasons in Major League Baseball ( MLB ) for the New York Yankees , from 1923 through 1939 . Gehrig was renowned for his prowess as a hitter and for his durability , a trait that earned him his nickname `` The Iron Horse '' . He was an All-Star seven consecutive times , a Triple Crown winner once , an American League ( AL ) Most Valuable Player twice , and a member of six World Series champion teams . He had a career .340 batting average , .632 slugging average , and a .447 on base average . He hit 493 home runs and had 1,995 runs batted in ( RBI ) . In 1939 , he was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame and was the first MLB player to have his uniform number ( 4 ) retired by a team . A native of New York City and attendee of Columbia University , Gehrig signed with the Yankees in 1923 .

Mike Timlin won the award in 2007 for his efforts in raising awareness and finding a cure for ALS , which took his mother 's life in 2002 .
